title: Office site of Dr. J. Marion Sims
alt: A 1994 Alabama Historical Association marker on a Montgomery street, titled Office Site of Dr. J. Marion Sims, “Father of Modern Gynecology”.
caption: The marker credits Sims with “successful operations for urinary fistula in women”. It does not name Anarcha, Lucy or Betsey.

title: The museum door
alt: In black and white, a member of the team stands in the doorway of a brick building, beneath a plaque to the surgeon Luther Leonidas Hill, with a Mothers of Gynecology museum sign inside.
caption: Two histories of surgery at one door: a plaque to Luther Leonidas Hill, the first American surgeon to suture the human heart, and the museum to the Mothers of Gynecology.

title: Layers

caption: Walls built over walls: older fabric showing through the newer city.

title: A brief history note
alt: A printed notice taped to a tiled wall, titled “A Brief History Note for those born after 1965 or Not from the South”.
caption: In the basement of a former shoe factory built in 1960, a notice explains why it has three bathrooms: one for white women, one for white men, and a smaller one for “colored”.
